posts.title: I Measured an Agent Gate Without a Model in the Loop. Here Is What It Catches, and What It Costs.
posts.description: The paper behind ReasonGate, now on Zenodo. A provenance gate on tool calls, measured by replaying the fully hijacked agent through AgentDojo with no model at all: attack success from 95.6% to 3.1%, 34 points of the user's own tasks as the price, what it costs in front of real MCP servers, the fourteen defects found in my own gate, a coverage map next to another gateway, and the model that did not

posts.title: Four Ways to Grow a Classifier, and Why the Safest One Cannot Learn
posts.description: My paper on arXiv: the obvious way to deepen a soft decision tree without changing its function leaves the new gates with a gradient that is exactly zero, not small, so the added level never learns. The proof, what it cost on Iris, Wine and Digits, why the cost is zero on two-class problems and tens of points on multi-class ones, and what the other three growth decisions actually buy.

posts.title: I Built neural-trees. It Is Ready for Other People. Here Is What It Does and What It Does Not.
posts.description: A scikit-learn compatible library of tree models that train by gradient descent: soft, multivariate and omnivariate trees, a hierarchical mixture of experts and a growing network. Every claim is regenerated in CI, every prediction comes with a path and a verified counterfactual, the model exports to JSON and ONNX, and the honest benchmark says where it loses.
